reaction: Their separate routes are clear in the model.

reaction: It's helpful that the hearing and balance parts share the same inner ear rather than being duplicated.

reaction: The shared vein connection makes sense without adding a duplicate.

reaction: The separate routes crossing between regions make the assembly clearer.

reaction: Seeing nerves and blood supply reach the same muscles ties earlier chapters together.

expectation: I expect the scarred segment to fill the forearm opening in the skin covering, ready to fit over the body.

reaction: The small scar staying in its original place ties the repair back to the whole body.
reason: I'll fit the skin covering over the assembled body; it's the only offered combination and completes the remaining goal.
expectation: I expect the covering to enclose the body while keeping its normal openings and repaired segment in place.

effect: The covering completes the body while retaining the repaired skin and the organs and connections assembled earlier. All goals are complete.
reaction: The final cutaway is a satisfying way to see the parts working together.

mostWorthwhile.text: Joining the head and spine to the trunk tied nerve signals and blood supply to the same muscles, bringing earlier ideas together.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the urinary organs was clear but felt like a routine placement rather than a particularly engaging decision.

surprise.text: I liked seeing that hearing and balance share the same inner ear instead of adding another one.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary: the slots and pictured connections explained the placements, though the compatible-action menu made them straightforward.

continue.text: I would probably continue to see more connections between systems, though another chapter made mostly of straightforward placements might feel repetitive.
